precepts.text: Sarai was barren from the beginning; she had no child.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
Sarah did not become barren in old age; she was barren from the beginning. “But Sarai was barren; she had no child.” Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age, and “it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.”

That is why she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. Barren from the start, and now past age. But is any thing too hard for the Lord?

precepts.text: The Most High makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
“Is any thing too hard for the Lord?” No. “He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.”

Sarah, barren from the beginning and past the manner of women, laughed at the thought of having pleasure after she was waxed old. The Most High answered the thought she never spoke, “Wherefore did Sarah laugh”, and when she denied it out of fear He said, “Nay; but thou didst laugh.” He sees what is within the mind, and He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children.

precepts.text: Through faith Sara received strength to conceive past age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised; of one as good as dead sprang as many as the stars.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
“Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed, and was delivered of a child when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.” She laughed at first, but she came to judge Him faithful, and nothing was too hard for the Lord.

“Therefore sprang there even of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.” Abraham was as good as dead at a hundred, and Sarah past age, and out of the two of them came a people that cannot be numbered.

precepts.text: Abraham considered not his own body now dead nor the deadness of Sarah's womb; he staggered not at the promise through unbelief.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
Abraham “considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara’s womb.” He was as good as dead, and it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women, yet “He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God”.

He was “fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform.” That is the answer to “Is any thing too hard for the Lord?” Sarah laughed within herself; Abraham was fully persuaded. And at the time appointed the Lord returned according to the time of life, and Sarah had a son.

precepts.text: The iniquity of Sodom: pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, and abomination committed before the Most High.
precepts.point: The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
What was the cry of Sodom, and what made their sin “very grievous”? Ezekiel lays it out: “Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.”

Pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, no hand for the poor and needy, haughtiness, and abomination. That is the cry that came up to the Lord before He went down to see it.

The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law. What the Lord took away as He saw good then, He sees again now.

precepts.text: Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain and pitched toward Sodom; his dwelling there is why Abraham interceded.
precepts.point: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
Why did Abraham draw near and negotiate with the Most High over Sodom? Because his nephew was there. “Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelled in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom.”

Lot’s dwelling there is why Abraham pleaded for the city. “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” He reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty and ten, and the Lord said, “I will not destroy it for ten’s sake.” Below ten there was no more negotiating; the Lord went His way, and Abraham returned unto his place.

precepts.text: I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. The Most High said, I know how Abraham gets down; he is not going to let his kids be out of order.
precepts.point: That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
The Lord told Eli, “them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.” Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself.

That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did. “For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.” The Most High said, I know how Abraham gets down; he is not going to let his kids be out of order. Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

Eli did the opposite. He honoured his sons above the Lord, and so the Lord said of his house, “Be it far from me.”

precepts.text: Sarah laughs within herself at the promise of a son because she and Abraham are old, and the Lord asks whether anything is too hard for him.
precepts.point: Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

precepts.why:
Abraham and Sarah “were old and well stricken in age”, and “Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?” The Lord answered, “Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.”

The Shunammite stands where our mother Sarah stood. She was a great woman who fed the man of God and made him a little chamber on the wall, and Elisha wanted to bless her: “thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for thee?” She had no child, and her husband was old. When Elisha told her, “About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son”, she did not believe it, just like Sarah: “Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.” The same words, “according to the time of life”, are in both promises.

And the same answer holds: nothing is too hard for the Lord. Sarah had her son, and “the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.”

precepts.text: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin very grievous.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.” He did that with Sodom and Gomorrah: “Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous”. The cry of their sin came up to him, and he looked down to see.

precepts.text: The Most High will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry of it.
precepts.point: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, that did seek God.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know.” The Most High goes down to see whether they have done according to the cry of it. That is God looking down from heaven upon the children of men, as Psalm 53 says, to see if any understand and seek him. He looked upon Sodom and Gomorrah the same way.

precepts.text: All the nations of the earth blessed in Abraham means the tribes of his seed, for Abraham did not father every nation.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?”

All nations blessed in Abraham means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth, for Abraham did not father every nation. The blessing of Abraham that comes on the Gentiles through Christ comes on the tribes of his seed.

points: Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him. Pause right there. This is what Bishop Yasab was saying to the men: it is up to you men to get your house in order. Do not wait for your wife to set it in order — if you wait for her, chances are it is not going to happen. You men must set your house in order.
And they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: And the Lord appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day; and he lift up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood by him. So listen to what it said. It said the Lord appeared unto him in Mamre, and then who came? Three men stood by him. So it was not physically the Most High God or the Messiah. The Lord could appear as men.
This is important because people are not understanding the secrets of how the scriptures are written. It said the Lord appeared unto him, but it was three men that came to him.

And when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground. There was something spiritual about these men, that when Abraham saw these three men he bowed down. The scriptures say the Lord appeared unto him through these three men.
And said, My Lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant. He called those men My Lord. There are three men. He calls those men My Lord.

Let a little water, I pray you, be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree. Come to my house. And I will fetch a morsel of bread, and comfort ye your hearts; after that ye shall pass on: for therefore are ye come to your servant. And they said, So do, as thou hast said.

And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes upon the hearth. And Abraham ran unto the herd. So imagine, you see these three men, you want them to come to your house, you are telling your wife, get food, get everything, get ready. Three men just came. These men are men of the Lord.

And fetcht a calf tender and good, and gave it unto a young man; and he hasted to dress it. And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they did eat.

And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him. He is talking with the men. She is listening in the tent, like, what is going on? What is all this commotion for? What are you all talking about?

Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age. They are almost a hundred years old. And look what the men of the Lord tell them. And it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women. She cannot have no baby at a hundred.

Therefore Sarah laughed within herself. So she was eavesdropping. They were not talking to her. They were talking to her husband and she was being nosy. It says she laughed within herself. She did not burst out laughing.

Saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also? This is what she is thinking in her head. He is old too. But just think — we were talking about health. I was doing the presentation for health at the men's conference and I was telling them, you should still be able to do it in your old age. Some of you all are forty, fifty, and you have got to pop a pill. Abraham was a hundred and still getting it in. A hundred and twenty, he was still having kids. So we are real far behind. And his wife still looked good at that age, because they still had the attraction to each other. They still had the desire. Some of you all are scoring away at thirty-five, forty, we do not do it any more.

And the Lord said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old? Remember, it says she laughed inside. And the man said, why is your wife laughing? She was outside the tent not minding her business. And they told them, check your wife, she is laughing. Because you all get mad when we tell you all stuff about your wives in here. And they did it right in front of our face. It said that she laughed within herself. She did not tell those men that.
Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.
Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not. She said, I did not laugh. Like she was trying to say the angels lied on her. For she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh. So you did laugh.

So the lie that Sarah told — I do not want to say a white lie, because it is still a lie, but she was afraid. She lied out of fear. Like Deacon Malachi said, in one of the schools we had a girl lie on one of the men. We had to go back and rewind the tape. She said that he touched her, and when we rewound the tape he was nowhere in her vicinity. That is the type of lie that Deacon Malachi is talking about. That is a wicked, despicable woman. When we rewound the tape, it was nothing like how she was saying. So you know that a seed of evil has been planted inside of you, if you sat down and you thought that up: I am going to tell them he touched me even though he did not touch me. And there are cameras all over to prove her wrong. That is a wicked person.

And the men rose up from thence, and looked toward Sodom, and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way. And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? Listen. The Lord came to tell Abraham that a child was going to be born at a hundred years old. But then they asked, shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? Destruction was coming. And they said, should we tell Abraham? Should we let him in on the secret? Because nobody knew that destruction was coming.
Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him? For I know him. He said, I know him.

That he will command his children and his household after him. He is going to keep his house in order. The reason why the Lord said, yeah, you could tell him what is going on, is: he is righteous, I know him, he is going to have his house in order, you can let him in on the secret. He is not going to let no wickedness go on in his house. So that is why we are the way we are with your families. The angels that came to his house had to ask the Lord, should we let him know the secret of what is about to go down? And the answer was, this guy is good, he keeps his house in order, he is going to command his family, I know him.
And they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.

And the Lord said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous; I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know. And the men turned their faces from thence, and went toward Sodom. So they walked away from Abraham to go to Sodom.

But Abraham stood yet before the Lord. And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? So they did not give him the information that everybody was going to get wiped out. And Abraham said, you are going to kill righteous people in the city also with the wicked?

Peradventure there be fifty righteous within the city. There are probably fifty people there that are walking in righteousness. The point that I am bringing out is, it is the same thing with us right now. We do not know who is keeping the commandments. We do not know who is in wickedness. Abraham thought that there were righteous people in the city, and there were none.

Wilt thou also destroy and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are therein? That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked: and that the righteous should be as the wicked, that be far from thee: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
And the Lord said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes. He said, I will not kill nobody if you could bring me fifty righteous.

And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, which am but dust and ashes: Peradventure there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: wilt thou destroy all the city for lack of five? And he said, If I find there forty and five, I will not destroy it. I will save it for forty-five people.
And he spake unto him yet again, and said, Peradventure there shall be forty found there. And he said, I will not do it for forty's sake. Notice he keeps lowering the number, and lowering the number.

And he said unto him, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: Peradventure there shall thirty be found there. And he said, I will not do it, if I find thirty there. And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: Peradventure there shall be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for twenty's sake.

And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: Peradventure ten shall be found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. And the Lord went his way, as soon as he had left communing with Abraham: and Abraham returned unto his place.

Three men stood by Abraham: these are angels. Did he run away from them like they were some demonic thing? No: he ran to meet them, bowed himself toward the ground, fetched water, and prepared food for them. Our forefathers never looked at these angels as something demonic that came down to persecute them. That is what Esau says, not what the Bible says.
